key_provisions_or_claims: Trust in human-robot interaction depends on reliability and ethical competence.
Robots cannot take the human moral stance, so ethical competence must be implemented via ethical algorithms.
Moral demands protect common goods and are universal and categorical.
Proposes a logical form of meta-ethical arguments as a pattern for programming ethical algorithms.
Approach is minimalist and not committed to a particular meta-ethical theory.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper proposing that autonomous robots need human-like ethical competence, implemented through ethical algorithms. It offers a model of the logical form of meta-ethical arguments, grounded in the human 'moral stance', as a pattern for programming ethical decision-making to support trust in human-robot interaction.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.title_en: Ethical Algorithms in Human-Robot-Interaction. A Proposal
annotation.venue: Computer Science & Information Technology (CS & IT), AIRCC
